title: Ducktective case file
description: The product. One JSON object per line in .ducktective/cases.jsonl, mirrored as Markdown for humans. Field names match skills/ducktective/SKILL.md — that file is the contract, this schema makes it checkable. Unknown keys are rejected: a misspelled field validates, then reads as undefined in the rap sheet.

covered.description: Line sites executed by the failing run; with --baseline, only the ones no passing run touched.

predicted.description: What the check must do if the hypothesis is TRUE. The oracle direction: the check should FAIL (crash, assert wrong) or PASS (behave correctly). run_check.mjs records this so the verdict is arithmetic, not prose.

check_exit_code.description: Exit code of the executed check. null = killed or never started, which can support no verdict.

control.description: Known-good command that must pass for the check to be a valid oracle (SKILL.md rule 5).

probe.description: How the accused location was neutered on a scratch worktree (`raise`/`throw` injected before the line), or null if never probed. The prediction and the control together only prove the check AGREES with the claim; a check that passes for reasons unrelated to the accused line survives both, so this is what makes `confirmed` mean something.

probe_exit_code.description: Exit code of the check with the accused location neutered. null = the probe could not be run.

probe_flipped.description: yes = the check's outcome changed when the accused line was neutered, so the check depends on it. no = it did not change, so the check proved nothing about that line (verdict: inconclusive_vacuous). not-run = never probed.

verified_exit_code.description: Exit code of the re-executed check (run_check --verify).

verified_verdict.description: What the second run would have concluded. Metric #2: a confirmed claim whose verified_verdict differs did not survive.

status.description: `open` exists so a mid-flight case can be persisted; SKILL.md forbids patching from it. A run that never executed is status `unverified` with the harness note in leading_hypothesis — `error` describes the reproduction, not the verdict.
